name: 4L Data Intelligence

quote: 4L Data Intelligence helps health plans reduce claims costs and operating expenses through patented Integr8 AI-powered payment integrity solutions.
identity_why: identifies() true. All three name tokens present in the identity fields - title is 'AI-Powered Health Plan Performance & Payment Integrity | 4ldata.com' and the meta description opens '4L Data Intelligence helps health plans...'
note: Confidence is medium on the BUYER, not the identity. Every buyer their own site names is a payer - 'health plans, TPAs, self-insureds, workers comp, Medicare and Medicaid plans'. It never names a state Medicaid agency. The exhibitor row's claim of 'government health programs' is not confirmed by the page. Category proposed on the Medicaid-plan line of business.

name: Argyle
description: Consumer-permissioned income, employment and asset verification APIs for mortgage and consumer lenders, tenant and background screeners, and government benefit-eligibility programs
quote: Government Benefits - Automate benefit eligibility more efficiently at scale
identity_why: identifies() true. Title is 'Argyle | Automate Income, Employment, and Asset Verifications' and the domain is the whole name (domain_is_lead), which is the exact-domain branch of the check; footer reads 'Argyle Systems Inc.'
note: NAME COLLISION CHECKED. getargyle.com also passes identifies() and is a different business - 'Argyle Consulting Services... a professional talent building team focused on resume services and career coaching'. Rejected. Government Benefits is one of six solution lines on argyle.com, which is why the category is medium, not high.

name: CSG Government Solutions
description: Program modernization consulting - project management, independent verification and validation, quality assurance and organizational change management - for state Medicaid, child welfare, child support, unemployment insurance and motor vehicle programs
quote: CSG Government Solutions modernizes large government programs with cutting-edge technology for a better user experience.
identity_why: identifies() true. Tokens 'csg' and 'government' both present; title is 'Your trusted advisor in government program modernization - CSG' and the meta description names 'CSG Government Solutions' in full.
note: Sector is medium because they are broader than HHS. Their own Program Expertise menu leads with Healthcare & Human Services, Child Welfare, Child Support - but also lists Unemployment Insurance, Workers' Compensation, Motor Vehicle, Revenue/Tax and Corrections. General Gov / Strategy & Performance is the defensible alternative. They are a consultancy, not a software vendor: no product is sold, services are.

quote: Codoxo builds AI solutions that help healthcare companies and agencies identify problems and act quickly to control costs with artificial intelligence.
identity_why: identifies() true. Single distinctive token 'codoxo' present in the title 'Codoxo: AI Solutions for Healthcare', and the domain is the whole name (domain_is_lead).
note: The state-agency buyer is asserted by the company itself, not inferred: their Markets menu is exactly three entries - 'Healthcare Payers / PBMs / State & Federal Agencies' - and the body reads 'trusted by top healthcare payers, government agencies, and pharmacy benefit managers'.

name: Datadog
description: Cloud observability, application monitoring and security SaaS for engineering and IT teams, offered to public agencies at FedRAMP High
quote: Unified Observability and Security. Now FedRAMP High
identity_why: identifies() true on both datadog.com and datadoghq.com (datadog.com resolves to the same 293KB document). Token 'datadog' present in the title 'Cloud Monitoring as a Service | Datadog'; the government page title is 'Government Monitoring Solutions | Datadog'.
note: NOT Health & Human Services. This is horizontal infrastructure that happens to have been in the room: the MESC 2026 exhibitor row reads 'Booth #311, Carahsoft Pavilion', i.e. present through a reseller's pavilion rather than as a Medicaid vendor. Nothing on their site sells to a health agency specifically. Category proposed on the observability platform itself.

name: EY
description: Audit, tax and consulting firm whose government and public sector practice advises agencies on program transformation and operations
quote: EY government and public sector consulting services provide support to transform programs and optimize operations to achieve better outcomes for the public.
identity_why: identifies() true on ey.com and on the government practice page. 'EY' is a two-letter name, so it clears only via the exact-domain branch (base 'ey' == the whole name) plus the title 'EY - US | Shape the future with confidence' and h1 'EY US - Home | Building a better working world'.
note: A two-letter name is the weakest thing this check can be handed - it cannot use the distinctive-word test at all. Accepted only because the domain IS the name and the h1 spells out 'EY US'. Sector is General Gov rather than HHS because EY is a generalist: the page that identifies them is the government and public sector practice, not a health one. Their Healthcare IT Connect 2026 row is 'Gold Community Sponsor' and names no product.

name: Equifax
description: Consumer credit bureau whose The Work Number service sells instant income and employment verification to state agencies determining SNAP, Medicaid and TANF eligibility
quote: Automate eligibility for SNAP, Medicaid, and TANF with income verifications. Access 145M+ active records updated every payroll cycle. FCRA-compliant data for government agencies.
identity_why: identifies() true on equifax.com (title 'Equifax | Credit Bureau | Check Your Credit', domain is the whole name) and on equifax.com/business/government/. The exhibitor list's URL - theworknumber.com/solutions/industries/government-verification - FAILS identifies(): that page is branded 'Government Employment & Income Verification | The Work Number' and the word Equifax appears nowhere in its title, meta or h1. The theworknumber.com HOMEPAGE does pass, because its title ends '| Equifax'.
note: Website moved from the exhibitor row's deep product page to the company's own domain, because the card names the company Equifax and the product page does not identify it. Sector is medium: Equifax is a credit bureau, and Benefits & Medicaid Systems is proposed on one product line (precedent: SteadyIQ, already filed there for the same job). General Gov / Suppliers & Services is the defensible alternative.

name: HLN Consulting

quote: HLN Consulting is a leading public health informatics consulting company that helps public health agencies modernize systems, improve interoperability, and strengthen decision-making.
identity_why: identifies() true. Both tokens 'hln' and 'consulting' present - title is 'HLN Consulting - Public Health Informatics and Open Source Experts' and the meta description names the company in full.
note: The exhibitor row's ICE claim is confirmed on their own site, not just in AIRA's directory: 'Open Source immunization evaluation and forecasting' is a section heading, alongside 'IIS on FHIR' and the domain list Immunization Information Systems (IIS), electronic case reporting (eCR), clinical decision support.

name: HealthTech Solutions
description: Medicaid systems modernization and integration, MITA/MECT certification support, program management, data warehouse and grant management consulting for state and federal health and human services agencies
quote: HealthTech is a trusted, approachable partner for many state and federal agencies and public and private organizations.
identity_why: identifies() FALSE, and the failure is the check's, not the company's. The site serves NO <title> and NO meta description, so the identity fields the check reads are empty ({present: [], missing: ['healthtech','solutions'], says: '.'}) and no page could ever pass. The company is named unambiguously in the body instead: 'At HealthTech Solutions, we believe our strength lies in the trust we place in our people', the footer 'HealthTech Solutions, LLC Copyright 2026', and a services page listing 'Medicaid Systems Modernization and Integration' and 'Alignment (e.g., MITA, MECT) to MECL using MECT for Outcomes Based (OBC) and Streamlined Modular (SMC) Certifications'.
fetch_note: add_company.fetch() returns 'unreachable: SSLError' - the server presents an incomplete certificate chain (CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED: unable to get local issuer certificate) on both healthtechsolutions.com and www. The site is live and serves 200 to a fetch with verification disabled, which is how it was read. Anything in the pipeline that trusts fetch() will record this company as unreachable forever until they fix the intermediate.
note: THE DANGEROUS NEAR-MISS. healthtechsolutions.net PASSES identifies() cleanly - title 'Home | Health Tech Solutions', tagline 'Innovative Diagnostic & Imaging Solutions' - and is a completely different business. Taking the domain the check approved would have filed a diagnostic imaging company as a state Medicaid consultancy. The MESC 2026 row ('Carahsoft partner, outside the Carahsoft Pavilion') and the .com site's own public-sector language are what settle it.

name: Innovaccer
description: Healthcare data and AI platform (Gravity) for providers, payers and life sciences, with a public sector line selling Medicaid analytics, case management and social health information exchange to state agencies
quote: public sector - Modernize Medicaid and public health for better outcomes
identity_why: identifies() FALSE. Their title, og:title and twitter:title are all 'The Agentic Cloud for Healthcare' and the meta description is 'Unify your data and deploy AI agents across clinical, operational, and financial workflows' - the brand name appears in NONE of the identity fields, so {present: [], missing: ['innovaccer']}. It is in the body repeatedly: 'About Innovaccer', 'Experience Innovaccer Gravity', 'Innovaccer Recognized by Black Book as a 2026 AI Leader', footer 'Innovaccer (c) 2026'.
fetch_note: Only the homepage is readable. /about-us returns 503, /public-sector returns 406, and www.innovaccer.com/public-sector times out - a bot wall, so the public sector detail could not be read beyond what the homepage nav and body carry.
note: Category rests on one line of homepage copy naming Medicaid, plus the nav items 'Social Health Information Exchange / Case Management / Medicaid Analytics'. Their four named industries are Provider, Payer, Public Sector, Life Sciences - public sector is a quarter of the business at most, so medium.

name: Jama Software

quote: Enabling a Streamlined and Collaborative Digital Workplace for Government and Public Service Missions

note: NAME COLLISION CHECKED. jama.io is a personal site belonging to a Jama Abdirahman and fails the check on the missing 'software' token; jama.com answers 403. Only jamasoftware.com is the company. NOT Health & Human Services: this is engineering requirements software whose government vertical is safety-critical programs, and the MESC 2026 row reads 'Carahsoft partner, outside the Carahsoft Pavilion' - present via a reseller, not as a Medicaid vendor.

quote: North Highland aids Health and Human Services in transformation, boosting agility and quality via ongoing improvement and strategic cost management.

note: Website recorded as the root rather than the exhibitor row's /industry-expertise/healthcare, because Healthcare and Health and Human Services are two separate industries in their own menu and the HHS one is the one that matches this conference sweep. Its h1 is 'Health and Human Services Consulting: Navigate Transformation with Confidence' and its featured articles are 'AI Governance in State Agencies' and 'Bridging the Gaps: Mastering End-to-End Testing in Modular Medicaid Ecosystems'. name: Performant, a Machinify company
description: Technology-enabled healthcare payment integrity - claims audit, eligibility and coordination of benefits, data mining and recovery analytics - for health plans, managed Medicaid plans and government agencies including the CMS RAC program
quote: Performant Healthcare Solutions technology-enabled audit, eligibility, recovery and data analytics solutions are designed to help health plans identify improper payments and recoup or save capital lost due to errant billing practices.
identity_why: Run it with the STORED name and both domains fail, in opposite directions - that is the whole finding. 'Performant, a Machinify company' against performantcorp.com: {present: ['performant'], missing: ['machinify']}. Against machinify.com: {present: ['machinify'], missing: ['performant']}. Neither page claims to be both companies, because no page is. Run it with the bare name 'Performant' and performantcorp.com passes cleanly - token in the title 'Home - Performant' and again in the h1 block 'Performant / Pioneering Payment Precision' - while machinify.com still fails with present: [], because the word Performant occurs nowhere in that document. The website recorded here is the one domain that identifies a company on this row.
acquisition: CONFIRMED, and the known pointer needs a correction. The brief says Performant points at machinify.com. It does not, yet: performantcorp.com is still live, still fully branded Performant, and carries its own banner 'Performant Joins Machinify - A new chapter in healthcare payment intelligence begins'. Recording machinify.com would file the parent brand's page against the subsidiary and would fail the identity check doing it, so the website here is performantcorp.com and the acquisition is recorded as a fact rather than papered over.
note: A THIRD DOMAIN IS A TRAP. performant.com is NOT this company - it is a UK consultancy, 'Performant is a trading name of Project People Limited, and specialises in contracted-out services'. Same shape as vocalis.net and kodex.com. Use performantcorp.com.

name: PwC
description: Audit, assurance, tax and consulting firm whose Health Industries practice advises healthcare, pharmaceutical, life sciences and medical device organizations
quote: PwC's Health Industries practice provides guidance in key areas impacting healthcare, pharmaceutical, life sciences and medical device organizations.
identity_why: identifies() true on pwc.com/us/en.html (title 'PwC: Audit and assurance, consulting and tax services', h1 'PwC US - Audit, assurance, tax and consulting services', domain is the whole name) and again on the Health Industries page titled 'Health Industries: PwC'.
note: THE EXHIBITOR ROW OVERSTATES WHAT THE SITE SAYS. The intake row credits PwC with 'health policy data and insights' for payers and providers; their Health Industries page names healthcare, pharma, life sciences and medical device organizations as the audience and does NOT name a state Medicaid agency, so the description was cut back to what the page supports. They exhibited at NAMPI 2026, a Medicaid program integrity conference, which is evidence of presence and not of a product. pwc.com/us/en/industries/government-public-services.html is a 404 - no US government practice page was reachable to read.

name: School of Lunch
description: Multi-day culinary training academy, school-food consulting and change toolkits helping school lunch programs and families move to scratch-cooked, nutrient-dense meals
quote: Led by fearless mom turned lunch lady Hilary Boynton, School of Lunch (SOL) seeks to revitalize humanity by empowering a global culinary movement to joyfully disrupt the trend of chronic illness.
identity_why: identifies() true. All three tokens present, title is bare 'School of Lunch', domain is the whole name, footer reads '(c) 2026 School Of Lunch. All Rights Reserved.'
scope_flag: REFUSED AS AN HHS / GOVTECH VENDOR - recommend scope review before intake. It is a real, readable organisation and the description above is what it sells, but it sells culinary training, consulting and toolkits to schools, chefs and families. There is no software, no state agency buyer, and no Medicaid or health-IT product. Its Healthcare IT Connect 2026 row is 'Corporate Community Sponsor', which buys a place on a sponsor list and is not evidence of selling to a state agency. The sector/category above are the least-wrong home IF someone insists on filing it, not a recommendation to file it.
note: Legal form unclear and NOT asserted. The site solicits donations - 'thanks to a nonprofit partnership, you can help us create a model program' - which reads as fiscal sponsorship of a program rather than proof the entity itself is a non-profit. Recorded as 'vendor' because that is what the page shows it doing; the kind should be checked against a registration before it matters.

Their /solutions/government page fails the check on its own (no title, no meta, h1 only 'Public service elevated'), which is why the homepage is the recorded website.

Both rejected. NOT Health & Human Services - address verification is horizontal data infrastructure; the Healthcare IT Connect 2026 row is 'Corporate Community Sponsor'. General Gov / Suppliers & Services is the defensible alternative to IT & AI Platforms.

name: StackAI
description: No-code platform for building, governing and deploying enterprise AI agents, sold to IT teams at organisations with regulated and complex operations
quote: StackAI empowers enterprises to deploy AI Agents at scale. Build secure, compliant AI applications in minutes with our intuitive drag-and-drop no-code platform.
identity_why: identifies() true. Token 'stackai' present in the title 'AI Agents for the Enterprise | StackAI' and the domain is the whole name. stack-ai.com and stackai.io serve the same document and also pass; stackai.net is a Spaceship for-sale listing and is correctly rejected by the parked-page guard.
acquisition: IN FLIGHT, and it is the top banner on their own site: 'Asana acquires StackAI - now every human-agent workflow runs in one place', with a second line 'StackAI Joins Asana to Build the Future of Agentic Work Management'. stackai.com is still fully StackAI-branded today. Expect this record to become an Asana brand; do not wire a job board to it without re-checking who owns the careers page.
note: NOT Health & Human Services. Horizontal AI tooling with no health or government product named anywhere on the page; their Healthcare IT Connect 2026 row is 'Corporate Community Sponsor'.

name: Truv
description: Consumer-permissioned income, employment and asset verification APIs for mortgage and consumer lenders, tenant and background screeners, and public sector agencies verifying wage-earner and self-employment income
quote: Build faster operating workflows with an income verification API powered by consumer-permissioned payroll, employment, and banking data.
